To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
We have studied the deflection of a proton beam by bent crystals in the CERN SPS.
We have demonstrated the feasibility of crystal-assisted collimation in the SPS for the LHC."
The crystal collimation system has been installed at the CERN-PS and has demonstrated the ability to deflect the beam with a 90 degree phase advance.
In summary, our research is concerned with

1) the investigation of the crystal deflection efficiency as a function of the beam parameters and crystal settings 2) the study of the beam losses induced by the crystal deflection in the collimator and the crystal itself 3) the measurement of the transverse distribution and angular spread of the deflected beam and the study of the crystal collimation efficiency as a function on these quantities 4) the study of beam halo and the beam emittance growth in the presence of a crystal 5
(i) the measurement of nuclear loss rates in the crystal; (ii) the measurement of the transverse distribution in the crystal; and (iii) the study of the collimation efficiency of the crystal.
the study of crystal-assisted collimation of high intensity beams.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the crystal collimation is a very promising technique for the LHC collimation system.
crystal assisted collimation has been demonstrated to be a feasible and efficient technique to collimate high intensity hadron beams.
the UA9 experiment has shown that crystals can be used to collimate the beam and the results obtained during the last run have demonstrated that the crystal collimation can be used in LHC.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
crystal collimation works well in coasting beam.
the UA9 experiment has been successful in demonstrating the feasibility of collimation with bent crystals in the SPS.
we have demonstrated the ability to control the crystal deflection and the collimator block intercept efficiency, and we have measured the beam halo and the collimation efficiency.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the crystal collimation in coasted beams is feasible and efficient.
the crystal collimator is capable to reduce the halo of the beam by a factor 10, and that the deflection efficiency of the collimator is very close to 100%.
the UA9 setup is capable to measure the deflected beam profile, to measure the nuclear losses induced by the beam halo in a collimator and to measure the collimator efficiency.
